newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan CPC signs $350 mln loan for Qatar plant.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan CPC signs $350 mln loan for Qatar plant.

text.p: Taiwan's state oil monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Wednesday it had signed a US$350 million syndicated loan to fund a joint-venture Qatar Fuel Additives Company (QAFAC) project.
Taiwan's Bank of Taiwan, First Commercial Bank, ChinaTrust Commercial Bank would be the lead underwriters for the $350 million syndicated loan, Chinese Petroleum said in a statement.
Japan's Sumitomo Corp, France's Paribas Bank also participated in the loan, it said.

Qatar's General Petroleum Corp owned 50 percent of the QAFAC's total stake, followed by Chinese Petroleum with 20 percent, Taiwan's Lee Chang Yung Corp with 15 percent and Canada's International Octane Ltd with 15 percent, the statement said.
The QAFAC project would build a petro plant which is expected to produce an annual 830,000 tonnes of methanol and 610,000 tonnes of methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE) from mid-1999.
The plant will be located in Messeid, 48 km (24 miles) off Doha, and is projected to use 100 million cubic feet per day of gas from the North Field and 500,000 tonnes per year of butane.
Gulf Arab state Qatar has the third largest gas reserves in the world.
